name: Ryan Detrick, CMT
zh_summary: @RyanDetrick says his contrarian call that the 9.1% Feb/March correction would be the year's largest pullback is holding, despite bulls cutting targets in July. This may be the earliest max peak to trough correction in a midterm year since 1958.
en_summary: @RyanDetrick says his contrarian call that the 9.1% Feb/March correction would be the year's largest pullback is holding, despite bulls cutting targets in July. This may be the earliest max peak to trough correction in a midterm year since 1958.
text:
One of our more contrarian calls was the 9.1% mild correction we saw in Feb/March would be the largest pullback of the year. We started to say that back in May and this wasn't a popular call. 

In July, many bulls were cutting their targets and calling for a bear market in Q3. The reasoning was midterm years tend to see the largest corrections.

This could now be the earliest max peak-to-trough correction in a midterm year since 1958.

text:

text:
A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.

Here's a full recap:

1. Q3 2026 earnings season got underway with reports from JPMorgan $JPM, Goldman Sachs $GS, Citigroup $C, and Wells Fargo $WFC, delivering a mixed but generally resilient picture for the banking sector. Goldman Sachs led the group with a standout quarter, posting its second-best revenue quarter ever as equities trading surged 72%, while Citigroup reported its strongest third quarter in a decade, driven by strength in services, wealth management, and equities. JPMorgan delivered a rare earnings miss despite raising its 2026 net interest income outlook, and Wells Fargo beat on earnings but missed on revenue. Across the sector, banks continued to describe the U.S. consumer as resilient, highlighted ongoing AI-driven corporate investment, raised or maintained optimistic net interest income expectations, and pointed to strong equity trading activity, while cautioning that sticky inflation, higher-for-longer interest rates, elevated valuations, and geopolitical risks remain key challenges heading into 2027.

2. Bank of America said 10-year U.S. Treasury yields may need to approach 6% before investors meaningfully rotate out of stocks and into bonds, according to its latest Global Fund Manager Survey. The survey found 76% of respondents expect the Fed to leave rates unchanged in October, while technology allocations climbed to their highest level since August 2020 and long semiconductors remained the market’s
